The Holy Mother. — You say well, my daughter, that the hospitals and the homes of the sick are for you the forecourt of Paradise!

If you, without sparing yourself, consume your life in them, they are for you Calvary, where, crucified by charity with your Jesus, with Him you will pass from the cross straight to Paradise.

The daughter. — This is indeed, my Mother, what I aspire to: to consume myself little by little, and even to contract some contagious illness while caring for them, and to die a martyr of charity. And this is the grace I hope to obtain from your immense maternal love.

How the conversation of the Daughters of Saint Anne with those outside who are not sick must be, so that it may be a virtuous and holy conversation.

§ I. With those outside who are not sick, in general.

  1. My daughter, my conversation with my neighbour was always a holy conversation; in them I beheld the image of the Heavenly Father; hence in conversing with them I conversed with my God. See the sun: as it advances over our world, instead of diminishing its light it goes on increasing it; so it was with me; my conversation served only to make me grow in holiness. My daughter, so that you may imitate me in this, and your conversation with the world, to which your vocation obliges you, may be a testimony to the holiness of your God, observe the following counsels which I give you.

  2. When some person from outside comes to visit you, you will not go to them without the leave of your Superior, who will assign you the companion who must always be at your side, hearing everything that is said to you. When the visit is over, you will both go and give an account of it to the Superior, telling her the conversations that were held.

  3. In these visits, if the persons are of the other sex, of whatever condition, lay people or priests, even close relatives (except your father), you will never allow them to touch your hand. If they are of the same sex, you will observe the courtesies that charity requires.

  4. To the person who visits you, even a close relative such as father or mother, you may not offer even a glass of water without the leave of your Superior.

  5. If the persons who visit you should propose some pious work to be done, e.g. to visit some sick person, to take in some girl in danger, you will stop the conversation, saying that you are not permitted to deal with such matters without the leave of your Superior.

  6. If during such visits you should receive some commission for one of your fellow sisters, you will not carry it out until you have first heard the Superior.

  7. Whatever you receive during such visits, when the visit is over you will bring to the Superior, who will do with it what she thinks best. If you receive notes, you will bring them to the Superior without reading them. If the person who hands them to you should show a wish that you read them, you will answer at once that this is not permitted to you without the leave of the Superior.

  8. If the persons who visit you are close to you, you will begin and end these visits with a Pater noster to me, your Holy Mother, said in common with them.

  9. You will receive these visits in the place appointed for it, and never elsewhere, without the leave of the Superior.

  10. You will never go out of the house without the leave of the Superior, and you will go out with the companion she assigns; and you will never go out alone. If for some necessity you should have to go out alone, the Superior will judge of this necessity.

  11. You will always go out and come in by the ordinary door of the House, and never by that of the Church or any other, unless you have the leave of the Superior.

  12. You will never go out at night; and before nightfall you will return home. If some necessity should require otherwise, your Superior will judge of such necessity.

  13. Going along the street, if you are in an inhabited place you will keep silence; if you are in uninhabited and solitary places, then you may converse in a very low voice.

  14. When you go along the street with your fellow sister, you will not let yourselves be stopped by anyone, of whatever condition, to talk. If someone should approach you for this purpose, you, while still walking, tell them that you cannot, and that they should come to the House if they have something to discuss. You will take nothing in the street, not even a letter, even if it were to deliver it to the Superior.

  15. It does not seem that you could ever have reason to pay visits to persons outside. If, however, this should be the case at some time, you will not pay them without the leave of your Superior, to whom you will tell the person you wish to visit and the reason for your visit. Throughout the time of your visit your companion will not leave you even for a moment. If the person should wish to draw you aside to speak with you alone, you will tell them, without human respect, that it is not permitted to you. And if you should have to speak alone, you will not do so unless, before going out, you have provided yourself with the express leave of your Superior; which leave you will never be permitted to presume. If the person with whom you wish to speak alone is of the other sex, you will not do this in a room with closed doors, but you will leave the door at least somewhat open; this is understood of any person whatever, except one’s own Bishop. And if the person should show a wish that the door be closed, you will say, without human respect, that it is not permitted to you.

  16. You will never take food outside the house without the leave of the Supe- [?] 17. When travelling, you will say to anyone who questions you and addresses conversation to you only those few words that charity requires; you will never take anything from anyone, not even by way of alms. On the journey you will try to occupy yourself with some good reading. If you have to dine on the journey, you will see that it is not with persons of the other sex. The senior in vocation will act as Superior on the journey, unless the Superior has arranged otherwise.

  17. When travelling, if you must stop in places where the Institute has a House, you will never be permitted to lodge anywhere but with your fellow sisters; not even with your relatives. During the time you stay in that House, even if only for one day, you will be subject to its Superior, and you will take part in all the common acts as if you belonged to that House.

  18. When Religious of another Institute are passing through a place where the Institute has a House and ask for lodging, the Superior will lodge them, giving them hospitality for three days and showing them every kind of attention.

  19. Whenever you lawfully hold conversation with your neighbour, it will be worthy of me, that is, necessary or useful, holy, and suited to the persons: you will not speak of worldly matters, matters of government, secular matters.

§ II. How the Daughters of Saint Anne must conduct themselves with their enemies.

  1. My daughter, listen attentively to the precepts that must govern your conduct towards your enemies. You must recognise no other enemies than those who would wish to draw you away from your God, who is your only good, and to lead you into sin, which is your only supreme evil: from these persons you will guard yourself well; you will always be watchful, especially when, by duty of your vocation, you have to deal with the other sex.

  2. Should it happen that, wrongly, or while you are entirely innocent, you are calumniated, persecuted, defamed, either in your own person, or in that of one of your fellow sisters, or in some community of the Institute, or in the whole Institute itself, in these cases you will guard well against any thought of revenge, against any curse, and even against any complaint: rather, in these calumnies, persecutions and defamations you will see occasions which the heavenly Father offers you of meriting greatly for Heaven. Hence you will thank, praise and bless Him for it with all your heart.

  3. You will sincerely love these enemies, calumniators and persecutors of yours, praying God for every spiritual and temporal good for them; and when the occasion presents itself and you have the strength, you will do them every good.

My daughter, the teachings you have heard thus far are very repugnant to nature, yet you will not be worthy of me unless you are exact in observing them. Jesus requires their observance of all Christians, with those words of the Gospel, namely: love your enemies; do good to those who hate you, and pray for your persecutors and calumniators; and He assures us that in this one is blessed, because the reward for it is abundant in Heaven. Of such enemies you will have no lack: you will find them even among those to whom you do good.

§ III. Conduct with the Doctor.

  1. Only the Superior may have the doctor called for the sick sisters.

  2. The Superior, or another deputed by her, together with the head infirmarian, will accompany the doctor to the sick sisters, and will never leave him for a moment.

  3. No one will be permitted to approach the doctor to say even one word to him without the leave of the Supe- [?]

§ IV. Conduct with the Confessor.

  1. My daughter, in your Confessor you will behold the person of Jesus Christ. With him you will conduct yourself with such modesty as not to know what face he has.

  2. You will not be permitted to confess to anyone other than the Confessor whom your superiors have assigned to you.

  3. You will not be permitted ever to converse with the Confessor outside the confessional without the leave of your Superior.

  4. When speaking with or meeting the Confessor, you will not kiss his hand, nor will you kiss the hand of any Priest.

  5. When speaking with your Confessor, even in the confessional, you will never use words of affection towards him.

  6. Neither with those outside nor with the sisters will you ever speak, either well or ill, of the present Confessor, nor of the confessors you have had in the past. Likewise you will take care not to say that you have no confidence in him.

  7. If you should have observations to make about the Confessor, you will make them to the Superior alone and to no one else.

  8. When some sick sister is to be confessed, it will be the Superior, or another deputed by her, who accompanies the Confessor there; and for the whole time the confession lasts, the said Superior, or the one deputed, will stay at such a distance that there is no danger of overhearing, but yet such that she can see the Confessor, and she will remain in prayer. When the confession is over, she will accompany him out. The same is to be said when he assists some dying sister.

  9. The rooms of the Sisters will have an enclosure as strict as that of monasteries of nuns; so that it will never be lawful to bring anyone into them, neither man nor woman, except in case of illness, in which case it will be permitted, out of necessity, to bring in the Confessor and the doctor.

Holy conversation which the Daughters of Saint Anne must have among themselves.

  1. My daughter, do you know what the coat of arms of my family must be? Fraternal love, with which my daughters must be united among themselves, so that they may be one heart and one soul, and it may be said that my whole Institute is but one single person. Paradise, as you know, is nothing other than the place of the love of God and of neighbour; and therefore my House, which was made up of me, your Mother, of my Spouse Joachim, your Father, and of Mary Immaculate, my Daughter and your first-born sister, was the true Paradise on earth, because the love of God and of neighbour had its seat there and rested there undisturbed. It was the only family in which, by reason of the person of my Mary Immaculate, the love of God and of neighbour could not fear even the least offence of an inadvertent venial sin. There was never in the world a family equal to ours in love, nor will there be in times to come. Indeed, I can tell you that not even the angels in Heaven, where they were created, had as much love as our Daughter Mary had in our House, because among them sin was able to enter; but not so in the heart of my Mary: she was confirmed in the grace that preserved her from any blemish of sin. Now, my daughter, I want you to know that my Institute is nothing other than an extension of my family: God has raised you up so that in you, fortunate ones, we may continue to live: I, your mother, Joachim, and Mary Immaculate.

You will therefore never be worthy daughters of mine unless among you the love of God and mutual love reach their fullness. Listen, then, to the precepts of this love.

  1. Mutual love is kindled, nourished and increased by observing those words of Jesus Christ which say: do to others what you would wish done to you; understood, that is, according to God. Hence, just as it pleases you that others adapt themselves to your way of seeing and to your wishes, so do towards your sisters; bear their faults readily without complaint; share in the tears, the troubles and the sorrows of your sisters, to lighten them by your compassion; rejoice in their good and in their joys; anticipate all of them in honour, in respect and in affability; be kindly and obliging with them; in a word, make yourself all to all, to help all to belong to Jesus Christ. All this is to be understood provided that you do nothing against the law of God, against your rules, or against the will of your superiors; otherwise it would not be true charity. From morning to evening seize every occasion that presents itself to do some service for your sisters.

  2. In your manner you will show reverence, beholding in your sisters the image of God and of me, your Holy Mother. When you have to call them, you will use the words: My sister, do me this or that charity; or else you will call them by their own name.

  3. Likeness serves mutual love; and so it is said: like loves like. Therefore, as far as lies in you, you will flee every singularity, whether in food, clothing, room, furnishings, or in the practices of piety: in a word, uniformity in everything; a uniformity which you will find without fail in the exact observance of the holy Rules.

  4. Take care, in order to foster holy charity, to have a heart that belongs equally to all your sisters; all have an equal right to your love, because all are daughters of one and the same mother. Hence you must flee the two vices of antipathies and of sympathies and particular friendships; these two vices truly kill unity, sow division, and bring death to holy union and to holy charity.

As soon as you feel that the devil wants to put some coldness into your heart, at once pray in a particular way for the one towards whom you feel it, and show her every kindness until you feel yourself free of it. Likewise take good care not to form a particular friendship with any of your fellow sisters, under any pretext whatever, whether of kinship, or of a shared office, or of holiness, etc. These friendships are the plague that brings death to holy charity and to holy purity. Hence the Superiors will keep watch over this matter, and when they perceive that someone is affected by this sickness, and shows signs of it by readily touching and embracing a fellow sister, or by secret conversations, then they will seriously admonish her to amend; and if the admonitions are of no avail, they will inexorably send her away from the company, without regard to any gift she may have.

  1. Love must make you all eyes, both to help your sisters to become holy and to preserve them from sin. Hence if by chance, and without your seeking it, you should happen to see some fellow sister of yours in danger of some grave failing; or should see that she has already fallen; or should notice that she is troubled by some grave anguish and grave temptation, or affliction; or even should see that, without scruple and habitually, she tramples on some Rule; in all these cases, at once, in a spirit of charity, and without saying a word of it to the offender or to anyone else, you will inform your Superior of it, so that, as a good Mother, she may apply a prompt and fitting remedy. And woe to you if, under pretext either of false humility, that you are more wretched than she, or that you have too many faults of your own to concern yourself with those of others; or for fear that the Superior will not keep you secret; or for fear of rousing the offender’s indignation against you, or for fear of being branded a spy, etc., you should keep silent [?] and not make it known; for all that evil and its consequences will be charged to you.

  2. If on some occasion you should offend and gravely displease a sister of yours, e.g. with a biting word, with an angry voice, with a severe and gloomy look, with a spiteful and uncivil shrug of the shoulders, with ironical words deliberately provoking in order to torment her and make her lose her patience (this is a vice truly of the devil, and worthy of being severely punished in whoever is frequently guilty of it), you will go as soon as you can to ask your Superior for a penance for these faults; and, if the Superior judges it good, you will go and ask pardon of your offended companion. You will do this act by kneeling before the one offended, who will also kneel, out of humility and as a sign that she forgives from her heart. They will not, however, touch or embrace one another as a sign of charity, unless this has been enjoined by the Superior.

  3. My daughter, the ill-guarded tongue is the cruel and murderous enemy of holy fraternal charity. Hence I want you to guard it, so that it does not go into words of murmuring, whispering and criticism. I want my daughters to have a particular abhorrence for this vice; and I want each one to pursue it in herself and in the others, so that it finds no place in any of my Houses.

  4. Hence I want a daughter of mine, when she has been guilty of a fault of murmuring, even small, even once only, even with a single companion, even in secret, to go as soon as she can to accuse herself of it frankly, and with all the circumstances, to her Superior, in order to receive a penance for it. And I want any of my daughters who has observed with certainty the said fault of murmuring in some fellow sister to inform the Superior of it as soon as she can.

  5. I want this precept observed with a quite particular scrupulousness if the murmuring and criticism have been against the superiors.

  6. Once a month (she will try to make it the 26th, the commemoration of my feast) the Superior will hold the conference on the vice of murmuring, in which she will inveigh against it with all her zeal; and in it she will call upon some sisters to tell the good sentiments and lights they have received from the Lord against that vice.

  7. Twice a month the Superior will hold chapter, in which the sisters in turn will accuse themselves publicly before her only of the faults of murmuring they have committed. On this occasion the Superior will call, at her discretion, two of the sisters, so that they may be told by the others, one after another, in a spirit of charity, of the faults of murmuring they have observed in them; and these two sisters will listen with humility to these admonitions, and then to the correction and the penance which the Superior thinks fit to impose on them. In particular, the said two sisters will kiss the feet of the others as a penance.

  8. Every morning, when the meditation is over, before leaving the Chapel, the Superior will say aloud: Sisters, let us guard ourselves today and always from the vice of murmuring.

  9. In every workroom there will be a small statue or image of me, your Holy Mother, at the foot of which, on a card in large letters, will be written: Glorious Saint Anne, our Mother, guard your daughters from the vice of murmuring.

  10. Every day, in turn, two sisters will receive Holy Communion in honour of my tongue and of the words I spoke in this life with my Daughter Mary Immaculate, so that she may preserve my Institute from the vice of murmuring.

  11. Once a week my daughters will make their meditation on the ugliness of the vice of murmuring and criticism, making strong resolutions never to commit it.

  12. Every month my daughters will make in common a day of retreat, in which one of the meditations and one of the practical examinations will be on the ugliness of the vice of murmuring.

  13. Every month my daughters will make a Triduum, each one privately, in honour of the holy conversations I held with my Immaculate Daughter, to obtain for themselves and for the whole Institute the grace of being always pure from the vice of murmuring.

  14. My daughter, if you wish to restrain your tongue so that it does not offend charity, accustom it to keep silence and to speak little. I want there to be two kinds of silence in my Institute. The one most strict; and of this my daughters will have one hour each day, during which hour they will not be permitted, wherever they may be, to say even one word without a real and rather grave necessity; and, granted this necessity, they will measure their words, so as to say only those that are necessary; and these words will be said in a voice as low as if they were saying them in the ear; I mean, as much as suffices to be understood. Likewise they will observe this most strict silence from the evening, at the hour of the Holy Rosary, until the following morning after the thanksgiving for Holy Communion, including the time of breakfast. In these times of most severe silence my daughters will all be as if mute, and my houses will be a sepulchre; and whoever visits them at these times should believe them deserted. Believe me, my daughter, this holy silence is so pleasing to me that you will not enjoy my intimate familiarity unless you are careful to give it to me exactly. Besides this very severe silence, there is another, milder one in my family; and this silence is to be observed throughout the day, except at the times of recreation, which is taken in common after dinner and after supper. This silence requires that you do not speak without some necessity; or, if you wish to speak when there is no necessity, then let your conversation be of holy and edifying things; and moreover, when speaking, it requires that you speak in a rather low voice, and only as much as suffices to be understood.

  15. You must distinguish not only the times for speaking but also the places. You will take care, then, never to say a word when you are in Church; and if you have to say a word, you will draw the person outside the Church; and if you have to listen, when someone approaches wishing to speak to you, you will, without human respect, draw her outside. Likewise you will observe a most rigorous silence in the Refectory. And if someone should lack something, it will be the care of the one sitting next to her to let the one serving know by a sign, so that she may provide it.

  16. You will observe silence by not speaking with those persons with whom you must not. Hence those of my daughters who have made their vows may not speak with the novices unless they first obtain the express leave of the Superior and of the mistress of novices.

  17. You will observe silence not only with the tongue but also with your whole person. You will take care, then, that when you are in your room, or going about the house, especially at night, you make no noise; and you will say the same when you close and open doors, etc.; you will take care that this be done without any sound at all.

  18. My daughter, so as not to fail in charity, you must govern your tongue at the time of recreation. First of all, you will all take recreation together after dinner and supper. And if for some reason you should not on some occasion be punctual in attending it, you will make your excuse to the Superior, giving her the reason for your delay. Likewise, if you should have to leave it, you will not do so without first asking the express leave of the Superior, telling her the reason for leaving.

This you must say of all the common acts, meditation, Mass, spiritual reading, from which you may not absent yourself even for a moment without the leave of the Superior.

  1. At the time of recreation, so as not to fail in charity, my daughters will try to hold conversations that both cheer and edify; and so for the most part their conversations will tend towards encouraging one another in virtue.

  2. In conversation, so as not to offend charity, you will guard against every kind of obstinacy in upholding your own judgement. If you are of a different opinion from the sister who is speaking, you will modestly put forward the reasons for your view, and then, whether they are accepted or rejected, you will remain at peace. You will take care not to interrupt rudely the sister who is speaking; you will not give offence with your words; nor will you ever show yourself offended by any word said to you. Take care also not to raise your voice too much.

  3. At the time of recreation you will take care never to talk about food, clothing and similar things; nor at that time will you bring up talk concerning the administration of the house.

  4. You will never bring to recreation the scandals you may have seen or heard in the hospitals or in the homes of the sick.

  5. At recreation you will take care never to speak unfavourably of this or that nation to which your sisters may belong.

  6. You will never bring up at recreation talk of the things of the world, e.g. matters of government, of wars, of marriages, of wills, of business.

  7. At recreation, and outside it too, you will never talk about the admonitions, the penances, the reproofs or the refusals received from the Superiors, whether received by you or by others, from Superiors living or dead. Likewise you will not bring into conversation the offences, the wrongs, the discourtesies you may ever have received from anyone.

Of all these things you may speak only with your Superiors.

  1. You will never be permitted to communicate the things of your spirit, such as temptations, afflictions, repugnances, faults committed, or spiritual consolations, penances, extraordinary graces, visions, revelations, to any fellow sister, under any pretext whatever, without the leave of the Superior. Nor may you speak of the penances or the extraordinary favours you may have observed in some fellow sister of yours, without the leave of the Superior. Likewise you will make no agreement with any fellow sister to admonish one another of your own faults, without the leave of the Superior.

ON THE SICK SISTERS.

32.° With the leave of the Superior you will each day take care to pay a visit to your sick fellow sisters, to whom you will render every service imaginable. You will show them compassion, letting them see that you share in their sufferings, and you will commend them to the Lord. You will then be watchful not to let yourself be tempted by the devil into thinking that the poor sick sometimes exaggerate their illness, or that they complain for want of mortification, or that they cannot be satisfied. And if there should be anything to say on these particulars, this will be the office of the infirmarian, to inform the Superior of it, who, as a Mother, will know how to speak with the sick.

CONDUCT OF THE SICK.

33.° When you are taken by some illness which you fear may become serious and send you to bed, you will inform the Superior of it, or else the Head Infirmarian. You will use no medicine without the leave of your Superior.

34.° My daughter, when you are sick, you will consider your bed as the cross of Jesus, from which by your example you preach all the virtues of the Christian, above all conformity to the will of the Lord, patience, long-suffering, obedience to the physicians of the body and of the soul, and to the infirmarians; so that to all those who visit you, you may be the good odour of Jesus Christ.

How the Daughters of Saint Anne are to conduct themselves with their Superior.

1.° My daughter, in my Institute the Superiors, beginning with the General and going down to those of each house, are my Vicegerents. I, then, am the Mother and the Superior who through them invisibly govern my daughters. Here, then, is your first duty towards your Superior: you will have an enlightened faith, which makes you see in her the representative of Jesus Christ, the source of all authority; and makes you see in her my minister. The Superior has her authority over you not by virtue of her natural gifts, e.g. of being a wise person, a capable person, a person who understands governing, and so on; nor even by virtue of her moral qualities, that is, of her prudence, her generosity, her affability, or of any holiness of hers whatsoever; no: but she holds her Superiority because she was lawfully elected to that office by one who had the authority to do so. Therefore, to find your Superior, you will take your eye off the creature and place it on Jesus Christ, from whom the creature receives her superiority. Thus you will see Jesus Christ, and me, in your Superior; and you will look upon your Superior in Jesus Christ and in me, your Holy Mother; and you will be persuaded that the authority of your Superior and that of Jesus Christ are, as regards you, one and the same authority. Know, then, and hold for certain, that the defects and the sins of which your Superior may be full do not in the least diminish her authority over you; and so they do not diminish in you the obligation of beholding your Superior in Jesus Christ and in me. You will therefore be well persuaded that your Superior is the mouth of Jesus Christ, through which alone, and in no other way, He makes known to you in your vocation, from morning to evening, what He wants of you. So that either you receive the divine will from the mouth of your Superior, or else you will be deprived of it, and from morning to evening you will do nothing but your own will, which is as much as to say that you will make no gain whatever for Heaven.

2.° My daughter, once you are well persuaded that only by means of your Superior can you have the divine will, which is as much as to say every true and only good for the acquiring of holy Paradise, from this persuasion it will follow that you will look upon her as your Mother, but a heavenly Mother, and not an earthly one; and you will have towards her a feeling of love, of gratitude and of divine reverence, strong and ever constant.

3.° You, my daughter, will show this love for your Superior by not letting a day go by without offering some prayer to the Lord for her in particular.

4.° You will show this love by taking part in all the sorrows, as in all the joys, of your Superior, in such a way that the suffering and the rejoicing of your Superior may be your own.

5.° Your filial love for your Superior will cause you to be pierced by her spiritual ills, so that when, without wishing to, you observe in her some defect by which God is offended, you will not be scandalised by it; no; but you will grieve over it as over an ill of your own, praying the Lord with tears to give her the grace to amend.

6.° You will show this true filial love of yours if, seeing her fall into some grave error, ruinous for her soul or ruinous for the family over which she presides, as if she were to let the observance of some Rule decline, e.g. the hour of rising in the morning, the length of the meditation, or were to change the uniformity in food and clothing, you will then, with promptness or secrecy, write of it to the Mother General, overcoming any fear of incurring the resentment of your Superior herself.

7.° You will show your love for your Superior by seeking to meet her pleasure in all things, as a testimony of the pleasure of your God, thinking, that is, that every time you give pleasure to your Superior you also give pleasure to your God; so that you may say to yourself: if in this or that other thing I please my Superior, I know for certain that I please my God as well.

A sign of this love of yours will be if you trample upon the temptation of jealousy, which might arise from your seeing that your Superior loved another more than you and preferred her to you. In these cases you will say sincerely within yourself: what pleases my Superior pleases me also; and it pleases me precisely for this reason, that it pleases her, and not for any motive of self-love. If, then, I see that it pleases my Superior to love another more than me, and to prefer her to me, this pleasure of hers pleases me too: and thereupon, overcoming and despising all jealousy, you will remain at peace.

8.° This filial love of yours must be accompanied by a feeling of reverence, by which you will guard against any low act of familiarity, such as touching her, embracing her, kissing her, and the like.

9.° This reverence will cause you, when you must go to speak with her, to revive your faith and say to yourself: now I am going to speak with the representative of Jesus Christ and of my Holy Mother.

10.° This reverence will cause you, when Satan stirs up within you some criticism of the conduct of your Superior, whether towards you or towards others, at once to take care to detest it and drive it away. Much more will you guard against making the least murmuring against her. And if some companion should have the boldness to murmur about her in your presence, you will turn your back on her as on a devil, and hold for certain that that tongue at that moment is moved by Satan.

11.° If for any reason it should seem to you that your Superior looked upon you with an ill eye, or that she spoke to you harshly and said humiliating words to you, you will consider yourself deserving of all these things and of worse, and you will receive them as from Jesus, who perhaps wishes to try you, or else is having you do penance for your sins; and you will never believe yourself entitled to show yourself offended by it, or to keep a sad face before her, and to answer her rudely and with a raised voice, or else no longer to approach her with the same frequency as before. You must conduct yourself just as I tell you, thinking that however much evil your self-love may seem to receive from your Superior, this evil is never so great as the good you receive from her, since from morning to evening she is to you the instrument of the divine will. Much more will you refrain from saying the smallest word to any sister about the harsh conduct your Superior shows towards you. And if your virtue were weak, and you could no longer bear the ill-treatment you seemed to receive from your Superior, then, either yourself or through whoever it may concern, you will with sincerity make everything known to the Superior General, begging her, if she thinks it good, to send you to another House. But I repeat to you: say not a word to anyone of your distress.

12.° Likewise you will never speak of the wrongs you believe you have received from your past Superiors.

13.° My daughter, in your Mother Superior you are to seek help and relief in all your distresses of spirit and of body. In particular you are to seek light from her to uncover the illusions of the devil. To this end you must know that Lucifer hides himself in a false light, so as to be taken for a good Angel; and this he does frequently.

You, then, so as not to be deceived by him, will do thus: when you feel urged to do things that are not ordinary, such as staying up at night to pray, abstaining from food, or similar penances, you will do nothing of the sort unless you first have the leave of your Superior. Likewise, if thoughts should pass through your mind that keep you agitated, gloomy, melancholy, of this too you will give an account to your Superior with frankness.

14.° When the Superior bids you, you will give her the account of your interior: this account you will give with the greatest sincerity and devotion, thinking that through it the Lord will have you draw much good for your soul. This account you will give in the form that will be prescribed for you.

15.° This sincere and devout account of your soul you will give once a year to the Mother General, either in writing or by word of mouth, as you are able.

16.° My daughter, these teachings which I have given you thus far on the way of conducting yourself with your Superiors, if you faithfully follow them, know that they will bring you to a most lofty holiness in your vocation. If you follow them, you will become so docile, pliant, humble, respectful of the least sign and of the intentions of your Superior, that you will remain wholly stripped of yourself, and you will live solely by the spirit of dependence, which is the spirit of Jesus Christ, and my spirit. Do not think, however, that you can arrive at the heroism of these teachings in a single day: they are so repugnant to fallen nature that to observe them requires so much violence as to make all self-love die of it; and therefore the saints say that the Religious life is a slow and bloody martyrdom. Courage! for I will help you.

My daughter, I exhort the superiors of my Institute that, if they should see one who had the very wicked spirit of criticism, of complaining about the conduct of the Superior, the very wicked spirit of speaking to her with haughtiness, of putting on a sad and restless face at every admonition she receives, they correct her seriously; and if, after being admonished, she does not amend, then they are to send her away from the Institute.

My daughter, behold how many beautiful virtues I have taught you to practise in your dealings with the various classes of your neighbours. They are all made to lead you to the acquiring of my spirit of Faith, Hope, Charity, Simplicity, Prudence, Humility and Meekness. All the acts of virtue that you can practise in dealing with your neighbour with the propriety he deserves are all hosts which, clothed in the light of Faith, in the longings of Hope, in the fire of Charity, and perfumed with the fragrances of Simplicity, Prudence, Humility and Meekness, united with my spirit, serve you to offer to God sacrifices of honour, of praise and of thanksgiving for all the graces, privileges and glory granted to me, your Holy Mother, and above all for the unique glory of having made me Mother of the Immaculate. And thus you attain ever better the gain of your vocation, which gain is that you be a perfect imitation of me, as I am of Jesus Christ and of my Immaculate Daughter, and that you be a victim continually offering herself to God in thanksgiving for all the great things He has wrought in me, your Holy Mother, and most of all for the singular crown of my motherhood; and in this way may you be my true, perfect and worthy Daughter, and worthily bear this Name, which is so great a glory for you before God, before the Angels, and before all the just of the Church! Now that I have instructed you how you can be virtuous in dealing with your neighbours, I will now disclose to you those virtues of Religion which you will have to put into practice in dealing with God and with me, your Holy Mother.

Devotion which the Daughters of Saint Anne must profess to her and to her Institute.

1.° My daughter, if you wish to see what your devotion and your love towards me ought to be, look attentively at your firstborn sister, and you will learn it. She never turns her eye from my face, just as I never take mine from hers. She sees in Me the one whom God took as His companion in order to give her being, and I in her behold, in a continual ecstasy of wonder, the plant from which the Fruit of the salvation of the world was to be gathered! So must it be with you; you are not to depart for a moment from my side. At every time, in every place, in whatever action you are occupied, you are never to lose my presence: you are always to think that the Mother and the daughter have but one life and one and the same heart. You, then, my daughter, will live by my life, think with my mind, will with my will, speak with my tongue, see with my eyes, hear with my hearing, and move with my movement. So, then, that through such a union you may rest continually upon my motherly bosom, hear the acts of devotion that I would wish from all my daughters.

2.° I would wish that on the 26th of every month they make the Commemoration of my feast; so that my feast may be celebrated by my daughters not just once a year, but every month. Before the said 26th day let them make my novena in common: and, if the finances of the House permit, throughout the novena they will give Benediction with the Most Blessed Sacrament. Then on the day of my commemoration they will have exposition, and so on that day they will have a sermon or a conference on some privilege of mine, or on some virtue of mine.

3.° My daughters, when they depart for a distant place, or arrive from one, embrace one another as a sign of charity, and give each other this greeting: Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate; and they answer: For ever be she blessed. Likewise, when they end the strict silence, this greeting must be the first word with which they break it. So too, on coming to the common recreation, the Superior, or whoever takes her place, begins it with this greeting; and with this greeting it is ended.

4.° At the striking of the hours I want my daughters to use the following ejaculatory prayer: My glorious Mother Saint Anne, make me devoted to Mary Immaculate, your Daughter.

5.° It pleases me that my daughters should continually carry on their person some devotion of mine, e.g. my medal, or a small picture of me, or a little image of me.

6.° My daughters, whenever they enter and leave their room, will take holy water, and then, partly kneeling before my image, will ask my blessing with this formula: Glorious Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate, and my mother, bless me. They will do the same when, for a lawful reason and with due permission, they enter one another’s room.

7.° Each of my daughters will take care to begin the principal actions of the day with this invocation: Saint Anne, Mother of Mary, and my Mother, obtain for me the grace to do everything for the glory of my God and of my Jesus.

8. Every conversation they have among themselves in private they will begin with a Gloria Patri to my most holy tongue, in memory of the holy conversations held with my Daughter Mary Immaculate.

9.° My daughters, whenever they meet about the house, greet one another with a slight bow of the head, and this in order to honour me, their Holy Mother, in themselves.

10.° After dinner and after supper, going to make the visit to the Most Blessed Sacrament for the Benefactors, they will say before my picture three Gloria Patri to my most holy tongue, to obtain the grace of not committing faults in the common recreation.

11.° My daughters in all their needs, common as well as private, spiritual as well as temporal, will have recourse to me, either with Novenas or with Triduums. Let my daughters beware of asking me for trifling things: let them ask me to grow in the love of God, in love for me and for their neighbour. When they ask me for temporal goods, such as to be healed of some infirmity, to have more talent for their employments, to be relieved of some interior pain, and the like, let the request always carry the condition: that is, if obtaining such temporal things will serve to make them ever more acceptable to God in their vocation. Let my daughter rest assured that if what she asks of me can help her to be more virtuous, more pleasing to Jesus, to Mary and to me, she will obtain it. And if, praying to me, she sees that she does not obtain it, let her bow her head and say: My Holy Mother sees that the thing I want is not expedient for me, at least for now: and let her remain at peace.

12.° In every workroom, and in every workshop, and in the room of common recreation, there will be a beautiful statue or Image of me; at its feet there will be a card bearing written the ejaculatory prayer: Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate, and my Mother, preserve me from the vice of murmuring.

13.° My daughters, in all the Houses of my Institute, will keep my month with great solemnity: and in the novena for my feast, if the number of the sisters permits, they will have Exposition.

14.° My daughter, if you wish your whole life to be as a perpetual act of devotion and of love towards me, do thus: consider yourself as a victim who, from morning to evening, by means of prayers, the observance of the Holy Rules, obedience and the labours of her own employment, is being consumed and sacrificing herself to God, united with my spirit, to thank Him for all the graces He has bestowed upon me, and above all for that of having made me Mother of Mary Immaculate, Grandmother of Jesus Christ, Spouse of Saint Joachim, and Mother-in-law of the glorious Saint Joseph; and for the glory which I now enjoy in Heaven.

15.° Your devotion and your love towards me would not be complete if you did not love your family with me; and with a great, strong and generous love. For you my Institute must be everything, because in it you are provided with every spiritual and temporal good. It is for you a royal road to all the holiness proper to your vocation: the Institute is your earthly Jerusalem, from which, going forth at the end of your days, you enter straight, and as upon a Chariot of Triumph, into the heavenly Jerusalem. Therefore the Institute must be to you your nation, your Homeland, your Kindred, Father, Mother and your very self. Hence you are to leave every name: the name of your Homeland, the name of your Family, and your very own name borne in the world, so as to keep no other name than the one the Institute gives you, of daughter of Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate, a Minim of Saint Francis of Assisi: so that, on entering the Institute, you may remain in it as one buried and unknown to the world.

16.° My daughter, in the morning, as you put on the habit, you will kiss it as a sign of love for the Institute: you will thank God for having called you to it, and you will fear making yourself unworthy of it by your infidelities. Of nothing will you be so afraid as of the loss of your vocation.

17.° But do you know, my daughter, which is the most sincere way of showing this love of yours for me and for my family? The exact observance of the Holy Rules. If anyone loves me, says Jesus Christ, he keeps my word. Here, then, is how to bear witness to your love for me and for the Institute: by the observance of the word that is written in this little book. Take care not to make a distinction between great Rules and small Rules; but you must strive to observe them all, because all are means that God has given you to reach the holiness of your state, to save your Soul with ease. Hence you will often draw from your breast burning desires to observe them all exactly. And if among them you should meet one that was repugnant to you, you will make these repugnances known to your Superior, so as to gain courage to overcome them; but you will not speak of them to any sister. And then it will help you to conquer them to think that in order to seize the Kingdom of Heaven, which is acquired precisely by observing the Rules, you must do yourself violence. And if you should meet some Confessor or Preacher who told you that you need not make so much scruple about not observing those Rules which do not touch the holy vows, because they do not bind under any sin, you answer him: Father, I do not wish to enter into this question: what I know is that if I do not exactly observe my Holy Rules, granted that I might still be a good Christian, I shall not, however, be able to be a good daughter of Saint Anne; which is the end for which God has called me into her family: and I know that whoever does not attain the end of her vocation is a useless person; and therefore, if I do not observe all my Holy Rules, I shall occupy the ground uselessly among the daughters of Saint Anne. And it is well known that the tree which occupies the ground without fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire. Therefore, Father, what I ask of your charity is that you reprove me for every failing against them, and spur me on to observe them all. Thus, my dear daughter, you will answer. And know, my dear daughter, that after the book of Holy Scripture there is no book so wholesome for my daughters as this one of my Rules. Indeed, this little book of mine contains nothing else but the word of God, which is written in the holy books, but chewed by me, your Mother, so as to make of it a food better suited to your stomachs, my little ones. In these Holy Rules you find milk for a little girl, and delicate food for your infancy, and solid food for your grown age. You have everything, then, in these Rules of mine to make yourself a saint, and a great saint. Of this book alone you have need, to be the one whom God wants you to be before His eyes, so as to crown you in due time with the crown of eternal glory.

18.° Now listen, my daughter, to some means that will help you to observe them well. 1.° You will ask your Superior to have a copy of them with you, to keep it always as a Relic. 2.° I charge the superiors that during the time of the novitiate they have the novice learn them by heart, like the Pater noster, and that they give her the understanding of them by explaining them to her. In this way she will have them always before her eyes all her life, as a mirror in which she may see all her steps, whether they are good or bad. 3.° Every two months they will be read in common. 4.° You will do a thing very pleasing to me if every morning in your meditation you call to review some little number of them, asking me for the understanding of it, and at the same time you make resolutions to observe it well. 5.° Every two months you will go to ask the Superior for a penance for the failings you may have committed against them. 6.° You will thank God for the grace He is granting you of observing them; and you will pray Him to continue this grace to you, and to grant it also to the whole Institute. 7.° In the morning you will put this question to yourself: Sister Anna, why have you come? You will answer yourself: I have come to honour my Mother Saint Anne by observing her Holy Rules. 8.° Every three months all the Rules of the various offices will be read in common, except those of the Superiors.

19.° So that my daughters may know that these Rules of mine are truly for them, they may not be given to be read to any outsider of whatever condition, except the Bishop of the Diocese in which the Institute has a house, without the express leave of the Superior General. To the Postulants, before they enter the Institute, the Superior, either herself or through another, will tell enough of them by word of mouth to make known to them the burdens of the Institute they wish to embrace. As soon as she has entered, and during the time of the holy exercises, she may read them.

Acts of Religion with which the Daughters of Saint Anne must converse with God.

1.° My daughter, you know that the objects of our Religion are: 1.° the Mystery of the Most Holy Trinity; 2.° the Mystery of the Incarnation; 3.° the Mystery of the Most Holy Mother of Jesus Christ, and our Mother, Mary Immaculate. My beloved, my House was the holiest Church that ever was in the world, because in it was Mary, who gave to God and to all His Mysteries the purest and most devout worship that a pure creature could give Him. You see, then, that the aforesaid Mysteries must be venerated in a singular way in my Institute. As for the Mystery of the Most Holy Trinity, always holding firm the dogma which teaches that the three divine Persons are one God only, and are among themselves in all and through all perfectly equal, you will nevertheless profess a special devotion to the Eternal Divine Father. This devotion you will show: 1.° by intimate and frequent acts of faith in those prerogatives which faith itself teaches us concerning this Divine Person, namely: that He is the first Person of the Most Holy Trinity; that He is the unbegotten Father; that He is the Eternal Father; that He is the Father of Our Lord Jesus Christ, who is a Son in all things equal to Him; that He is the Principle of the Son and of the Holy Spirit; that He is the one who gave us His Divine Son, that He might redeem us from sin; that He together with His Son has sent us the Holy Spirit, that He might sanctify us; that He is the almighty Father, who has created all things, has providence over all, and leads all things to their last end. 2. You will show your devotion to the Eternal Father by invoking Him frequently during the day with one of the aforesaid Names, saying, e.g.: O Eternal Father! another time: O Father of my Jesus! another time: O almighty Father, Principle of all things! another time: O Father of my Soul, my Love, my Heart, my life, my providence, my treasure, my grace, my happiness in time and in eternity. 3.° In your necessities you will sometimes make a Novena or a Triduum to Him, with firm confidence that you will obtain all that is truly good for you.

2.° Your worship and your love for your Jesus will be truly singular.

His Infancy, His Life, His Passion will be the ordinary subjects of your meditations. You will always carry His Image on your person: at every free moment your eyes will at once be upon the Image of your Jesus Crucified. You will strive to bear His Passion in your body by means of bodily penances.

3.° Therefore, although, in view of the heavy labours of the active life, your Rule does not impose great bodily penances on you, you will nevertheless hold them in great esteem, you will always have a great desire for them; and if your bodily and moral strength permit you, you may also perform them in the measure that will be allowed you by your Superior, from whom you will first ask leave. In particular all my daughters will practise the following mortifications. 1.° On all the Wednesdays of my month there will be strict abstinence. So too on all the Wednesdays of the month of March, in honour of my Son-in-law Saint Joseph; the Houses with Hospitals are excepted, in which they will keep simple abstinence. Likewise on the eighth day of every month there will be no fruit at table: this small mortification will be in memory of the definition of the Immaculate Conception, which took place on that day. So too in the Houses that have no Hospital, on the last two days of carnival they will keep strict abstinence; and where they have a Hospital they will keep simple abstinence. This mortification will be to give some recompense to the Lord, who in those days is so greatly offended by the excesses of a great part of Christians. Thus you will honour the humiliations of your Jesus Crucified with the small humiliation of the Chapter, in which you will publicly confess your faults of murmuring, and will also be publicly admonished for them.

4.° You will have a special devotion to Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament, and you will show it by the following acts: 1.° you will hear Holy Mass every day; 2.° you will be prepared to receive Holy Communion every day, as far as it is possible for you; 3.° in order to have your soul always pure, and to be disposed each day to lodge your Jesus in your heart, every eight days you will wash yourself in His Divine Blood in the Sacrament of Penance; 4.° every day you will make the visit to the Most Blessed Sacrament for the length of time fixed by the superiors; 5.° every time you must go out of the House, immediately beforehand you will make a brief visit to Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament, to entrust your Heart to Him, that He may guard it during that going out of yours; and as soon as you have returned you will go back to Him, to make Him an act of thanksgiving for the assistance He will have given you; 6.° during the day you will strive to honour Him frequently with mental visits or spiritual Communions; 7.° when travelling and stopping in some place, if you are able, the first thing will be to make a visit to Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament. 8.° You must know that the Spirit of my Institute is that in all those Houses where there are sufficient means and members, perpetual adoration be made, so that as often as possible the exposition of the Forty Hours, or of a whole day, be held; and where there are no means, and there are not enough members, perpetual adoration be made with the Tabernacle closed.

5.° My daughter, the name you bear is enough to let you know that your love towards Mary Immaculate must be without measure. If I were to tell you that every breath of yours must be an act of love for her, I would not have told you too much. All the persons who come near you must feel the flames of your love for her; in short, love her as your Mother, and as your firstborn Sister, with that love with which I myself loved her.

6.° To honour that continual prayer, meditation and most lofty contemplation of mine, which kept me intimately united to God and transformed in Him, every day you will make three quarters of an hour of meditation in the morning, and half an hour in the afternoon. This meditation will be made in common and, as far as possible, before Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament. Every day you will recite the Holy Rosary in common, and other prayers established by the superiors.

7.° To rise each day more from purity to purity, from virtue to virtue, my Daughters will make the particular examen before dinner in common, and will make the examen of the whole day in the evening before going to rest. The length of these examens will be fixed by the superiors.

8.° Likewise every day they will nourish their Souls with spiritual reading made in common. So too, for the whole time of the meal, so that with the body the soul may also be nourished, they will read some good book: there will never be a day in the year, not even that of my feast, on which this Rule is dispensed.

9.° Once a week the Superior will give her Family a spiritual Conference: this conference will for the most part be on some point of the Rule.

10.° To honour that long and holy solitude of mine, in which I prepared myself to become the worthy Mother of the Immaculate Mother of my God, my daughters will make eight days of spiritual retreat every year. The novices will have, in addition, five days during the year, in honour of my five joys.

Behold, my daughter, the completion of that holy edifice which you must raise up in your soul, in my family, into which God has caused you to be born: whenever you have come to be filled with my Spirit of Faith, of Hope, of Charity, of Simplicity, of Prudence, of Humility and of Meekness; whenever, in order to attain the fullness of this spirit, you have detached yourself from possessions through holy Poverty; from the pleasures of the senses through holy Chastity, Modesty and detachment from your Relatives; from yourself through holy Obedience; whenever, in order to attain the said spirit, you converse virtuously and in charity with your neighbour, with the sick, with outsiders in general, with your enemies, with the Physician, with your Confessor, with your Fellow Sisters, with your Superiors; whenever, in order to perfect yourself in the aforesaid spirit, you are religious towards me, your Holy Mother, and towards your God, then you will be a perfect and true daughter of mine; you will be holy with that holiness which your God required of you in calling you to my Institute. Then you will have offered in yourself that sacrifice of honour, of praise, of thanksgiving to the Most Holy Trinity for all the wonders of grace wrought in me for Its glory, and above all for preparing me to be the worthy Mother of Its very own Mother, Mary Immaculate. But the Lord wishes to lead you to this most lofty holiness in my House, and under my motherly care, also so that you may be fruitful in holiness in your neighbours: God wants you holy, and wants you as a means of the sanctification of others. Attend, then, with diligence to the functions that serve you to attain this second gain of your vocation.

Functions of the Daughters of Saint Anne for sanctifying their neighbour.

§. 1.° Classes of persons entrusted to them.

1.° My daughter, my Institute is called to the succour of poor girls in danger. By girls in danger are meant all those poor girls who, not being watched over in their own homes, would sooner or later run the risk of losing their innocence, and above all the angelic virtue. Therefore I open my Houses to these doves in danger, so that in them they may find a refuge; I provide them with every temporal need; I provide them with lodging, food, clothing, and everything that life requires. I teach them all those works befitting their sex and condition. I give them that intellectual, moral and religious formation which serves to make of them persons useful to society, perfect and holy Christians; so that, fleeing vice, fulfilling their duties, loving God and their neighbour, they may attain eternal life. But, my daughter, in all this work I make use of you and of all your Fellow Sisters. You, then, are to behold these girls as the jewels of my family. Therefore you are to nourish for them great esteem and great love. This esteem you must show by keeping towards them a bearing full of respect, avoiding in your speech all those words that are harsh, imperious, and that savour of what is low and uncivil; and you will call them by the name of my dear daughter, or else by their own name, using gentle manners, but far from excessive familiarity. Your love you will show by accepting with pleasure from your superiors those offices which concern their good, e.g. teaching them school, teaching them to read and write, good manners, and works befitting their condition; assisting at their acts of Religion; seeing to their cleanliness, etc. You will show it by praying for them, being solicitous that they flee every offence against God, that they love and respect one another as good sisters. In particular it will be very dear to your heart to lead them, by example and by words, to a tender devotion towards me, to be grateful to me for the continual benefit I do them in keeping them in my house, feeding them, clothing them and educating them as my beloved little daughters; and to offer me their prayers often, so that I may without ceasing enrich them with the Treasure of my graces and make saints of them.

2.° In particular you will show yourself truly a Mother to them in their illnesses: you will serve them unsparingly in the manner that will be assigned to you by your Superior: you will not tire of procuring for them every bodily and spiritual relief. In a word, I want you to be all eyes, to procure for them every innocent consolation; because in this way they will see in you a Mother of theirs who, as though forgetful of herself, thinks only of making them happy: once persuaded that you are wholly for their happiness, they then give themselves entirely and without reserve to your exhortations to leave evil and do good, and to your corrections to amend the evil already done; and in this way you make them all mine, all my Mary’s, all my Jesus’, all God’s, all holy.

3.° Furthermore, my daughters must use the most rich treasure of my graces to sanctify the sick in the hospitals and the sick in their homes. How many of these, my daughter, go to their death badly, without thinking of the interests of their soul! You, then, my daughter, to draw them out of this blindness and eternal ruin, do you know what I want you to do? I want you to devote yourself wholly to serving them and relieving them in their bodily ills, and this with great sacrifice on your part; because, to serve them well, and to procure for them both bodily and spiritual healing, you must spare no toil; it must not grieve you to render them the services most nauseating to nature, to spend whole days and entire nights at their bedsides; to suffer there heat, cold, hunger and discomforts of every kind; in a word, to wear out your health and your life to save theirs. Giving yourself in this way to their bodily good, you will succeed in making them enter into themselves, so that they may provide for their spiritual good. In this you will imitate your Creator, who in the earthly Paradise fashioned our body in order to breathe His spirit into it; you will imitate Jesus Christ, who, healing the sick of every kind of bodily disease, healed them at the same time also of the diseases of the spirit, that is, of sin. So it will be with you: the sick person, seeing that for his benefit you take so little account of your health and of your temporal life, will open his eyes and come out of that error, namely that there is no other happiness than that of health and bodily pleasures, and will begin to be convinced that there must be another happiness, far better and eternal, for love of which you so little prize the temporal life. Likewise, seeing you wholly occupied in his relief, he becomes persuaded that you are a person who truly loves him and wishes him true happiness; and therefore he begins to esteem you, and then begins to esteem that Religion and that Jesus Christ for love of whom you labour so much for him; he begins to hold you and your words in veneration; hence he willingly accepts your exhortations, with which you exhort him to think of his soul, to receive the Sacraments, to have patience, to unite his death to that of Jesus Christ, and to trust in His divine mercy, to hope firmly for Paradise, and to long ardently to be united with Him in eternal life. And thus his eternal salvation is accomplished. Behold, my daughter, you have come to the point where you gather in full the fruit of your Holy Vocation; which fruit is, first, to sanctify yourself, and second, to help your neighbour to sanctify himself.

But I want to warn you that here, if you go out, as it were, from yourself, and are almost forgetful of yourself in order to attend to the sanctification of your neighbour, you must not remain outside yourself; but you are bound to re-enter; which is as much as to say that the holiness you procure in others must fall back upon yourself, and by the very work with which you sanctify others you are to sanctify yourself. And to this end I suggest to you here some means.

§. 2.° Means which the Daughters of Saint Anne must use in order to exercise virtuously their functions towards their neighbours, and in general all their actions.

1.° My daughter, in order that in the functions you exercise towards your neighbour, and in general in your actions, you may be truly virtuous, two conditions are needed: 1.° that they be functions and actions which please God; 2.° that the pleasure of God be precisely what moves you to do them; then it is that it will be said of you what is said of Jesus Christ in the Holy Gospel, namely that He has done all things well. Now, the first condition is not lacking to any of your functions; you may rest assured that all that is prescribed for you in these my rules is good. It remains only that you, with the grace of God, add the second; that is, that you accomplish everything solely to meet the pleasure of God. The pleasure of God is every good in heaven and on earth; therefore whoever succeeds in giving delight to God attains every good, the infinite good, the pure good. This endeavour to seek the pleasure of God in all actions is called purity of intention: when you, my daughter, in the functions you carry out for the good of your neighbour, have nothing else before your eyes but to meet in them the pleasure of your God; when this pleasure of your God is the only target, the only goal, towards which you direct all your heart, all your love, all yourself and all your activity, so as to rest in it fully; then it will be said that your intention is most pure. Consider well, my daughter, that this purity of intention in your activity is the only light that can illumine and adorn your works; it is the only gold that can make them precious in the eyes of your God, that can make them deserving of reward with Him. Now take note that this purity of intention has two fierce enemies, and these enemies are: seeking, when you act, your own satisfaction, or else seeking the satisfaction of the creature, so as to rest your heart in it. If, then, when you set about doing some action good and upright in itself, what draws you [?] to it is nothing more than satisfying yourself, or the pleasure of some creature loved by you, then for that action, though good in itself, you would have no reward to expect from your God. Indeed, in this case it may happen that such an action is so tainted by these crooked intentions that it is changed into an evil one and deserves punishment. In every action of yours, at its beginning, in its progress and at its end, look carefully about you, that the aforesaid two defects in no way enter into your intention of doing it for the delight and glory of God; for otherwise, if you mixed them with it, it would remain contaminated in some part, and your action would lose its worth. So that you may succeed in defending yourself from the aforenamed enemies of Purity of intention, who are always at your side, I want to give you some signs by which to look them well in the face and recognise them; and so always repel their assaults.

2.° First sign. If, when you begin an action of yours, or in the middle of it, or after you have already finished it, you should feel rising from the depths of your concupiscence a feeling of complacency in yourself, in your ability, in your talent, then know that your own satisfaction, the pleasure in yourself, the enemy of Purity of intention, is standing at the door to enter and contaminate it. You will at once be ready to detest such an evil feeling; and to crush it you will use the weapon of that divine word which teaches us that all honour and glory is due to our God, and that to us wretched ones nothing belongs but confusion. Likewise if, while doing or having already done some function for the benefit of your neighbour, e.g. having served with complete self-denial a most loathsome sick person, a most tiresome sick person who cannot be satisfied, or having carried out a piece of work with perfection, with the approval, honour and applause of men, you should feel at that moment that there rises within you a relish, a pleasure in such approval; that relishing, pleasurable feeling of your fallen nature must make you aware that human respect, the satisfaction of men, the second enemy of Purity of intention, is trying to taint it for you. Use promptly against this human respect the consideration of those words of Jesus Christ, which are terrible to those who seek human glory, and which say that in His judgement He will say to such people: go, and expect no reward from me; for you have already received it from men. Likewise, if, as it seems to you, your action turned out with the disapproval of men, with their contempt, and on this account there arose in you a strong regret, a sadness, a melancholy that would like to dishearten you, take hold of yourself at once; for all this is the work of pride, which would have it that in that activity of yours you had aimed at the satisfaction of men and at their esteem. To overcome this most wicked feeling of sadness, remember that you must take no account of pleasing men in your actions; but you must love and prize only the pleasure of your God, and being approved by Him. And if such disheartenment should seek to sustain itself with the excuse that you are at fault, that the function went badly, dispel this excuse by thinking that in these cases God calls you to the sense of your own nothingness, to the refuge of holy Humility, which does indeed confess its own fault, but with calm, without losing confidence and without losing heart; indeed, the more it feels its own weakness, the stronger it feels itself in the grace of its God and in the divine mercy. Take care, however, that under pretext of not putting yourself in danger of growing vain, or of bringing contempt upon yourself, you do not perform your public duties badly and with negligence; for this would be an illusion of the devil; it would be folly, and subtle pride.

3.° Second sign. Another signal for perceiving whether in your functions Purity of intention has been touched by its aforesaid enemies is to pay attention to yourself, whether you give yourself up somewhat to the feeling of jealousy and envy on seeing that other Institutes similar to yours are held in greater esteem, enjoy love and sympathy more than yours; that it is said that they carry out their functions better, e.g. that they educate their boarders better, that they take more care of them, that they keep them cleaner, better mannered, etc.; if you gave yourself up, even a little, to such movements of envy, fear indeed that in your activity you are not seeking purely the pleasure of your God and to glorify Him; but are seeking in some part yourself and the creature; because if you loved only the pleasure of your God, seeing that it pleases God that other Institutes be esteemed and loved, be approved and praised in their undertakings, it would please you also. Therefore, my daughter, nourish a holy horror of such movements of jealousy and envy, which always come from cowardice and baseness of spirit; be glad that all Institutes are happy and prosperous in everything.

4.° Another signal, akin to the preceding one, is excessive solicitude in procuring virtue in those persons who will be entrusted to you; a solicitude that leads you to be unable to tolerate the least defects in them; to correct them continually, and with harshness. Hold for certain, my daughter, that this spirit hides the two enemies of Purity of intention; because in the virtue of the persons given into your care it does not aim only at the pleasure that your God finds in it, but in addition it wants that splendour which gratifies its own eyes and the eyes of others. And in a defect it is not displeased only that God is offended by it; no; but it flees the shame that comes to it from men, as though the faults and the imperfections of the persons subject to it were poured back upon it. Be careful, then, to employ all your strength in the sanctification both of yourself and of the others entrusted to you; but with calm, being fully persuaded that you, with your toil and your sweat, turn the soil, but the growth of the tree and the ripening of the fruits come wholly from Heaven.

5.° Finally, my dear daughter, guard yourself against sloth, which also is a daughter of the two enemies of Purity of intention. When you, my dear daughter, in your practices, above all those of religion, are not eager to do them well, but are listless, are lazy, move with difficulty, what does this mean? It means that you do not have at heart to be that soil where God finds His delights, gathering there the fruits of virtue; to be that most beautiful image in which He with infinite complacency beholds Himself; it means, in a word, that in those practices of yours you are not seeking purely to give delight to your God; which is as much as to say: you do not have Purity of intention in them. What drags you to do them is the fear you have that, if you do not do them, God will punish you with temporal scourges and then send you to hell: which means that in them you are seeking yourself and your own interest. For charity’s sake, my daughter, take care not to be slothful: for in this way you would be unfaithful to the covenant which, on entering my Institute, you made with God. He, in the act of granting you this grace, leading you within, made a covenant with you that, in gratitude for so great a benefit, you would always be an object of His delights and of His good pleasure. If, then, you make this expectation of His vain, you run the risk of incurring the curse threatened against souls that defraud Him.

6.° Lastly, my daughter, I want to point out to you a means of defending yourself effectively from the two enemies of Purity of intention, of whom I have spoken to you thus far: this means is that you never, either in one another’s presence or in absence, praise one another for those gifts which are purely natural goods and which of themselves serve nothing to make you saints, e.g. for the ability to teach school, to carry out women’s work, for manners and outward bearing, for the ability to succeed in the various employments of the Institute, as Superior, sub-superior, Bursar and the like. As for virtues, you must never praise one another in each other’s presence. And if some sister is worthy of praise for her heroic virtues, and this sister is absent, it will be lawful sometimes, rarely and sparingly, to speak of some act of virtue of hers, of humility, of meekness, of charity in the service of the sick, and this in order to be edified and encouraged by her example. Likewise I do not want you to blame any of your sisters for lack of natural endowments, nor because she is timid and fearful with the sick, nor because she has little ability for school; if in these matters there were need, for anyone, of a curb on her vanity or of encouragement for her faint-heartedness, these tasks will belong to your Superior. My daughter, thus far I believe I have spoken to you enough for you to know who I am, and for you to understand how you must think and act in my Institute, so as to call yourself and to be in truth my daughter. In this little book of mine I have given you a most strong tower, in which to place in safety all the duties of a good Christian. Know, my dear daughter, that a Christian who keeps his mind, his will and his works within the compass of the 12 Articles of the Creed, within the compass of the Ten Commandments, of the seven petitions contained in the Pater noster, and in the due use of the seven Sacraments, is a Christian just, holy and blameless in the eyes of God, and worthy of eternal life. Now the fourteen Chapters which make up these Rules of mine are as fourteen walls, which defend you from failing against the said duties of the Christian. If you do what is written in them, you will never be in danger of going astray in any article of the creed: the fire of love towards God and towards your neighbour, which is as it were divided into ten flames in the ten Commandments, will always be alight in your heart; likewise the seven longings of the Pater noster will be continually alive; and you will make holy use of the seven fountains of living water, which are the Holy Sacraments. Furthermore, my daughter, in these fourteen Chapters you have all the holiness of the evangelical counsels. In the observance of these fourteen Chapters you have victims to offer continually to the Lord in thanksgiving for my privileges, above all for the graces received in the nine months during which I bore the Immaculate in my most holy womb, and for my Five Joys. My daughter, courage then: I will be with you to help you observe these holy Rules of mine; and when you have observed them, you will sing the Hymn of holy Humility, saying: O my God, behold your useless servant: in observing these holy Rules of yours I have done only what was my strict duty; indeed I have done nothing; but it is your grace in me and with me that has done everything. Therefore to You, my God, One and Three, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, through my Lord Jesus Christ, be all glory for ever and ever. Amen.

THE END
